dedupe_keys.name: peering simulation game isp peering and transit negotiation

description: The Peering Simulation Game is a live role-playing simulation that teaches how Internet service providers negotiate peering. Four audience members act as ISP peering coordinators in a fictional Internet called BillLand, each starting with USD 35,000 of venture funding, rolling dice and growing their network by acquiring customer squares on a virtual board; they earn money per square and pay monthly transit fees to one of two upstream transit providers. By negotiating peering they cut transit costs, and because ISPs both cooperate to reduce costs and compete to maximise their bank accounts, the game reproduces peering negotiations similar to real ones. The game is based on the research 'Internet Service Providers and Peering' and 'A Business Case for Peering', has evolved since 2002 and has been run in over 40 international forums on five continents, including AfrISPA IXP training in more than 18 countries. Producer: William B. Norton of DrPeering, in the Internet Peering Playbook. Coverage: conceptual, not tied to a country. Access: a free white paper giving the game and its rules with lessons learned. Licence and cost: free to read, no licence stated. Caveats: it is a teaching game, not a calibrated network model, and includes no software. Simulation uses: it illustrates agent-based negotiation between networks at exchange points. Related record: DE-CIX traffic statistics (data-de-cix-traffic-statistics) for real exchange traffic.
